actualTrackingIssueBody:
# HTTP.sys connection-close append: focused lookup reduction

Fork-only research tracking for retained finding **F046**.

The shared internal `HeaderCollection.Append` does a dictionary read and write.
Use one `CollectionsMarshal.GetValueRefOrAddDefault` slot only for the exact
Dictionary runtime type; keep original interface operations for wrappers and
subclasses, existing guards, comparer, key spelling, order, and null semantics.

The actual inspected shipping caller is HTTP.sys `Response.ComputeHeaders`
appending `Connection: close`, not general application/request-header append.
IIS compiles the class and passes managed contracts but has no references to
this method in the inspected managed owner IL; native IIS is not validated.

**Qualified focused local result, not merge-ready:** primary median **13.41%
less time**, all three pairs faster, **384 B/op unchanged**. This small suffix
includes the real collection's construction/setup, one compiled delegate call,
one close append, and count readback. Native HTTP.sys/IIS/application throughput
and production frequency are not measured.

The unchanged same-profile control median is -0.96%, with primary exceeding it
in all three pairs. Keep adverse/shared-machine evidence prominent: the
unchanged KeepAlive secondary control swings 27.44% in pair 2, the WrappedStore
fallback regresses 2.31% in pair 3, and the largest case CV is 13.46%.
No fallback improvement or allocation saving is claimed.

# [AutoPerf F046] Avoid duplicate HTTP.sys close-header lookups

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

<!-- If this is your first PR in the ASP.NET Core repo, please run through the checklist
below to ensure a smooth review and merge process for your PR. -->

- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).

- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

Avoid a second dictionary lookup when appending HTTP.sys close headers

## Description

**Fork-only draft for retained finding F046; qualified focused local efficiency,
not merge-ready.** This targets the shared internal `HeaderCollection.Append`
used by HTTP.sys `Response.ComputeHeaders` to append `Connection: close`.
It does not optimize general application/request-header extension calls.

Use `CollectionsMarshal.GetValueRefOrAddDefault` only for the **exact**
Dictionary runtime type. All guards retain their order; wrappers and subclasses
retain the original interface read/concat/write fallback. Comparer, original key
spelling, concatenation order, and present-empty null semantics are preserved.
No constructor, field-type, public/protected API, dependency, new friend-assembly,
or unsafe-accessor changes are introduced.

### Measured result and limits

The declared fresh default-store primary takes **13.41% less time** by median
paired effect: **9.44%, 16.85%, 13.41%**, at **384 B/op unchanged**. The unchanged
same-profile extension control has a -0.96% median effect; the primary exceeds it
in every pair. Three AB/BA/AB source comparisons are permanently closed.

This is a roughly 10-19 ns saving in a fresh response-preparation suffix that
includes collection construction, setup writes, a compiled delegate call, close
append, and count readback. Neither native HTTP.sys/IIS throughput, production
frequency, nor application impact is measured.

**Adverse/noisy results remain prominent:** the unchanged KeepAlive extension
control appears 27.44% faster in pair 2, exceeding that pair's 21.84% native
secondary effect; WrappedStore is 2.31% slower in pair 3 and has no claimed
improvement. The largest case CV is 13.46%. All samples and controls are retained,
not treated as isolated-hardware or formal statistical-significance results.

### Connected evidence

| Artifact | Link |
|---|---|
| Tracking | jaslawinMs/aspnetcore#160 |
| Exact two-file source | [Source commit](https://github.com/jaslawinMs/aspnetcore/commit/4b84f010b923c6dd7154d5a3cc19dc0b17874bbc) |
| Scope, classification, equivalence, test map, and limitations | [Immutable guide](https://github.com/jaslawinMs/aspnetcore/blob/fbe9899664bc10dc6dfe66e6de7e8835709671f9/F046/README.md) |
| Runnable nine-file BenchmarkDotNet project | [Project](https://github.com/jaslawinMs/aspnetcore/blob/fbe9899664bc10dc6dfe66e6de7e8835709671f9/F046/harness/AutoPerf.Benchmarks.csproj) |
| All comparisons, variance, allocations, and raw results | [Results](https://github.com/jaslawinMs/aspnetcore/blob/fbe9899664bc10dc6dfe66e6de7e8835709671f9/F046/comparison-results.md) |
| Exact commands, outcomes, and preserved preparation failures | [Validation](https://github.com/jaslawinMs/aspnetcore/blob/fbe9899664bc10dc6dfe66e6de7e8835709671f9/F046/validation-commands.md) |
| Source/results arithmetic and XML audit | [Audit](https://github.com/jaslawinMs/aspnetcore/blob/fbe9899664bc10dc6dfe66e6de7e8835709671f9/F046/audit-summary.json) |

Actual owner IL establishes one HTTP.sys `ComputeHeaders` call site and no
references in the inspected managed IIS owner. Six real native HTTP.sys profiles
observe both managed post-producer state and client protocol/header/body output;
IIS validation is managed shared-class contracts, **not native IIS integration**.

Original and candidate each pass **10 owning unit rows and 5 existing native
functional rows**, with every parameterized XML row checked and zero skips.
The actual current-default owners are built and characterized separately.
The independent nine-file project restore/rebuild repeats both variants with
20 owner contracts, 12 fresh boundaries, and 6 native profiles each, without
another timing run. The audit reconstructs **576 samples**, **22 runtime records**,
and **144 per-benchmark settings records**.

The initial original-only fixture run had three incorrect expectations, corrected
before shipping edits or timing; all failed inputs and streams are retained.
This is green/green preservation, not a semantic-bug red/green claim.
Native IIS, JS/static assets, packaging, full-repository and application-throughput
validation are not claimed. Physical snapshot/PDB hashes bind the measured body;
the later publication commit is not passed off as its original compiler input.

The immutable evidence snapshot predates its additive publication receipt. The [current case guide](https://github.com/jaslawinMs/aspnetcore/blob/autoperf-results/F046/README.md) connects the later issue/PR/browser receipt without changing any of the 879 sealed core files.

Each fresh shell activated its checkout first; complete streams and the untimed reconstruction commands are linked above.
